## Dataset expanded to 130 prompts across 16 families

The original 13 tasks were too few to characterise coding capability. The dataset is now **130 tasks**, and the families were **derived from this repository's own history** rather than invented — `git log --name-only` over the last 200 commits ranks the edited areas as `src/`, `tests/unit/`, `data/seed/`, `changelog.d/`, `.github/workflows/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `data/meta/`, and the commit-subject distribution is docs > test > fix > chore > feat. The dataset mirrors that shape, so it measures the edits we actually make.

[Dataset + generator gist](https://gist.github.com/konard/6a71a4b3afa86c977575465135e2f391) · in-repo at `experiments/issue_847_coding_ladder/`.

### By level

| Level | Shape | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Whole issue → pull request (the Hive Mind `solve` shape) | 16 |
| L2 | One coherent deliverable | 12 |
| L3 | One concrete edit, location named | 28 |
| L4 | One atomic operation on one named file | 74 |

### By family

| Family | N | Example prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `atomic_edit` | 22 | In this repository, in scripts/detect-code-changes.rs, add "dev/log/" to the excluded_folders array. |
| `read` | 12 | In this repository, read src/proof_engine/types.rs and list the variants of the ProofOutcome enum. |
| `multilingual` | 11 | Создай файл src/ladder_ru.rs с одной публичной функцией на Rust с именем ladder_ru… |
| `search` | 8 | In this repository, find where the string example.org is emitted as evidence and tell me the file name. |
| `knowledge` | 8 | What triggers a new version release in this repository? |
| `test_authoring` | 8 | Create a Rust test file tests/unit/ladder_evidence.rs containing one test asserting example.org does not appear in src/solver.rs. |
| `targeted_edit` | 7 | In scripts/detect-code-changes.rs, make docs-changed respect the excluded_folders list. |
| `create` | 6 | Create a new file src/si_units.rs containing a single public Rust function millimetres_to_metres… |
| `decomposition` | 6 | Split this coding task into at least two smaller independent subtasks, numbered list only… |
| `replace_delete` | 5 | In src/solver.rs, replace the hard-coded fetched_at value 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z with a call to current_timestamp. |
| `deliverable` | 5 | Add a paths-ignore filter for experiments/**, dev/log/** and docs/case-studies/** to release.yml. |
| `verification` | 5 | Run cargo check on this repository and tell me whether it succeeds. |
| `multifile` | 4 | Create src/ladder_units.rs with a public function and register the module in src/lib.rs. |
| `error_recovery` | 4 | Run cargo check. If it reports any error, tell me the file and line of the first one. |
| `refactor` | 3 | In src/web_search_core.rs, rename WEB_SEARCH_RRF_K to WEB_SEARCH_FUSION_K everywhere in this file. |
| `issue_to_pr` | 16 | Solve GitHub issue …/issues/846 in this repository and open a pull request with the fix. |

### What the expansion deliberately covers

- **Every artifact type we actually touch**, not just Rust: `.rs`, `.lino`, `.md`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.sh`, `.json`, plus `changelog.d/` fragments and `.gitignore`.
- **Replacement and deletion as distinct from insertion** — agents commonly append where they were asked to replace, and that failure is invisible if the dataset only tests insertion.
- **Multi-file, dependency-ordered work** (create a module *and* register it in `lib.rs`), the shape most real fixes take.
- **Repository knowledge** — the questions a developer asks *before* editing ("where do unit tests live?", "what triggers a release?").
- **Error recovery** — reacting to a failing build, which is where a real `solve` run spends most of its turns.
- **The same coding intents in ru/hi/zh**, since the #386 convention requires identical routing across supported languages.
- **16 L1 issue→PR ceilings**, one per real open issue with no PR, so the corpus grows naturally as issues are filed.

Anchors are verified: all 130 IDs unique, all `verify` snippets pass `sh -n`, and every referenced file exists except the four that creation tasks are supposed to create.

`prompts.json` is generated by `generate_prompts.py` — edit the generator, not the JSON, so the dataset stays reproducible and its provenance stays legible.

The 130-task baseline run is in progress; I will post the measured numbers when it completes. The 13-task baseline reported in this issue's body (2/13, both passes read-only, zero writes at any level) still stands as the last full measurement.

## Measured baseline on the 130-task dataset: 38/130

`main` @ v0.303.0, agent CLI 0.25.0, driven through `formal-ai with agent`.

```
TOTAL 38/130
  L1 0/16    L2 0/12    L3 3/28    L4 35/74
```

### By family

| Family | Passed |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | 12/12 |
| `atomic_edit` | 6/22 |
| `knowledge` | 4/8 |
| `verification` | 4/5 |
| `create` | 3/6 |
| `multilingual` | 3/11 |
| `decomposition` | 2/6 |
| `error_recovery` | 2/4 |
| `search` | 1/8 |
| `replace_delete` | 1/5 |
| `issue_to_pr` | 0/16 |
| `test_authoring` | 0/8 |
| `targeted_edit` | 0/7 |
| `deliverable` | 0/5 |
| `multifile` | 0/4 |
| `refactor` | 0/3 |

### This corrects the 2/13 conclusion in the issue body

The 13-task sample said "no level where Formal AI can write code." That was **too small a sample and partly wrong**. Writes do succeed — 10 of 60 write tasks pass. What the larger dataset shows is a sharp boundary the small one could not see:

**Every passing write is "append a line to a prose or config file"** — `.md`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.lino`, `.sh`, `.gitignore`. `edit.readme_line`, `edit.workflow_comment`, `edit.compose_comment`, `create.doc_file`, `create.lino_seed`, `replace.replace_prior` (a numeric constant swap).

**Zero writes produce valid code.** `test_authoring` 0/8, `targeted_edit` 0/7, `refactor` 0/3, `multifile` 0/4, `deliverable` 0/5.

So the capability boundary is not level, it is **artifact kind**: text insertion works, code generation does not. That is a far more actionable finding than "nothing works," and only visible with enough breadth across artifact types — which is exactly what the expansion was for.

`read` at 12/12 is genuinely solid; navigation is not the bottleneck. `search` at 1/8 is the surprise: locating a symbol fails where reading a named file succeeds.

### A verification defect this run exposed

The first 130-task run reported **49/130 with `test_authoring` at 7/8**. Those were false passes. Asked for a Rust test file, the agent creates the file whose entire content is the echoed prompt fragment:

```
$ cat tests/unit/ladder_spotcheck.rs
one Rust test named ladder_spec_probe asserting the crate version string is not empty.
```

A `grep` for the test name passes on that. The runner now requires any `.rs` file a task was asked to create to contain an `fn` item — the cheapest structural check separating code from echoed prose. **10 tasks were reclassified from pass to fail**, and `test_authoring` went 7/8 → 0/8.

This is the fifth instance in this ladder of the same lesson, and it is worth stating as a rule for any harness in this repo: **substring assertions on agent output are not verification.** A file that exists is not a file with correct content; a command that was emitted is not a command that worked. Same root failure as #832 closing "verified" before #838 arrived with an empty body.

### Definition of done, updated

- [ ] A generated `.rs` file contains compiling Rust, not the prompt echoed back.
- [ ] `test_authoring` > 0 — the second most common commit type in this repository.
- [ ] `targeted_edit` > 0 — editing existing code, not just appending to prose.
- [ ] `search` approaches `read` (12/12); locating a symbol should not be harder than reading a named file.
- [ ] `multilingual` approaches its English equivalents (3/11 today) per the #386 convention.
- [ ] L2 and L3 non-zero before L1 is attempted seriously.
- [ ] The 130-task score is recorded per run so regressions are visible.

Dataset and generator: [gist](https://gist.github.com/konard/6a71a4b3afa86c977575465135e2f391) · `experiments/issue_847_coding_ladder/`.
